name: Dropbox
summary: The original sync folder: files that follow you between devices, with shared folders and links layered on top.

factors: Shared folders with clients and collaborators who also use Dropbox
Share links sent out over the years, which will stop working
Paper documents, which are not ordinary files
Camera uploads and computer backups that quietly depend on it

export.summary: Files are ordinary files: sync or copy them out. Paper documents and anything kept online-only need a little extra care.

methods.name: Sync client
methods.detail: Mark the whole Dropbox folder as available offline, wait for the sync to finish, then copy the folder elsewhere. Simple, but it needs enough local disk space.

methods.name: rclone
methods.detail: Copies directly from Dropbox to another cloud or server without passing through your laptop, and can resume after an interruption.

caveats: Paper documents sync as link files, not content: export the ones that matter as Word or Markdown
Online-only files are placeholders until they have been downloaded
Files in folders that other people shared with you copy out, but the sharing does not
Team folders on business plans may need an administrator to export
Version history and deleted-file recovery stay behind

paths.verdict: The like-for-like replacement when you share folders and links with other people.

import.summary: Copy the files into the Nextcloud sync folder, or use rclone to move them server-to-server over WebDAV. Recreate shared folders and links afterwards.

transfers: Access from desktop, web and phone
Camera uploads, through the Nextcloud phone app
lost: Existing share links and shared-folder memberships
Dropbox's sync speed on very large folders

paths.verdict: The closest match to Dropbox's sync speed, for people who want a file platform and nothing more.

import.summary: Create libraries that mirror your top-level folders, then copy the files in through the sync client or with rclone's Seafile backend.

transfers: Access from desktop, web and phone
On-demand files through the drive client
lost: Existing share links and shared-folder memberships
The surrounding apps that Nextcloud would give you

paths.verdict: A good match if Dropbox was only ever your own folder on several computers, and you never send links.

import.summary: Let Dropbox finish syncing on one computer, move the folder out of Dropbox, share it in Syncthing and pair your other devices. There is no upload step because there is no server.

lost: Shared folders with people outside your own devices
On-demand files: every device holds a full copy unless you exclude folders
A proper mobile experience on iOS

paths.verdict: A lighter, files-only alternative to Nextcloud. Young, so better suited to teams happy to be early than to ones that need a long track record.

import.summary: Copy the files into the desktop client's sync folder, or use rclone to move them server-to-server over WebDAV. Recreate shares afterwards.

transfers: Access from desktop, web and phone
lost: Existing share links and shared-folder memberships
